body:
## Problem

PR #666 (#623) makes a fold stop before pushing when taking the base in would remove a bundle's work from the line. Its PR body lists known limits (`results/issue_623/pr-description.md`, "Known limits"). Two of them are real gaps where the fold does **not** stop, and no issue tracks them:

1. **Detection is per file and starts at the cut point.** If the base partially reverts a file that another change also touched, or reverts work below the line's cut point, the check doesn't see it. The revert reaches the line silently.
2. **The revert comes in through a later bundle's own branch.** A later bundle whose branch was cut from a base that already holds the revert brings the revert onto the line when it is folded. #666 covers only the base merge, so this path is outside it.

The other two limits fail safe (the fold stops, and only the message differs), so they are not part of this issue.

## Done when

Decide, for each gap, whether to detect it (for example, compare the line before and after **every** merge in a fold, base or bundle, against all work on the line) or to document it as accepted in `docs/07-crosscutting.md`. Each decision is pinned by a real-git test or by a documented limit.

Relates to #623, #631, #633. Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-10 (issue_623 PR "Known limits").
title: stack mode: revert detection (#623) misses partial/below-cut-point reverts and a revert brought in by a later bundle's branch
